steps.thinkAloud: First: what kind of thing is a planet? "A thing" is too broad, and so is "something in space". The closest group is celestial bodies that don't make their own light: opaque celestial bodies.
What looks like a planet but isn't one? A star shines in the night sky too, but a star makes its own light. A planet only reflects it.

item.note: a star makes its own light; a planet only reflects it

steps.thinkAloud: Something closer: Pluto, a dwarf planet. It orbits the Sun and it's round, so what's missing? It hasn't cleared the other objects out of its path.
Now, what does something need to count as a planet? It has to orbit a star.
It needs enough mass for its own gravity to pull it into a round shape.

item.value: round because of its own gravity

steps.thinkAloud: And it has cleared its orbit. That's the one Pluto was missing.
Last: what kinds of planets are there? Rocky ones like Earth and Mars.
And giant ones made mostly of gas or ice, like Jupiter and Neptune.
